We cover Milwaukee because it matters. Full stop.

The Ledger Room is a small, independent magazine publishing original reporting on Milwaukee's politics, food, arts, and neighborhood history. We are funded entirely by our readers. We have no corporate owner, no investor, and no editorial mandate beyond getting things right.

✦

Why we exist

Milwaukee has had its share of headlines — a major American city with a complex history, deep inequalities, extraordinary creative energy, and a food culture that refuses to be simplified. What it has not always had is journalism that treats it with the seriousness it deserves.

The Ledger Room started in 2019 as a newsletter, written by two former newspaper reporters who were tired of watching local coverage shrink. It grew into a weekly publication with a staff of six writers, a podcast, a print quarterly, and a community of readers who have made it financially viable without a single outside investment.

We cover the city's politics without access journalism. We review restaurants without PR relationships. We write about the neighborhoods being reshaped by development — sometimes with residents' consent, sometimes without it — and about the neighborhoods that have already been erased. We believe that the history of a city is not a sidebar; it is the story itself.

Everything we publish is available without a paywall. Membership funds the reporting. If you read us regularly, we'd be grateful if you joined.

Contributors

Nadia Okafor

Editor in Chief, Politics

Nadia co-founded The Ledger Room in 2019 after seven years at the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel, where she covered city hall. She's a Milwaukee native, a graduate of Marquette University, and the recipient of a 2024 Wisconsin Newspaper Association award for investigative reporting.

Marcus Trzeciak

Senior Reporter, Politics & Housing

Marcus co-founded The Ledger Room after a decade covering urban policy at newspapers in Chicago and Cleveland. He covers city government, housing, and the land use decisions that shape Milwaukee's neighborhoods. He lives in Bay View.

Jess Halvorsen

Food Editor

Jess has been writing about food in Milwaukee for twelve years. She came to The Ledger Room from a previous stint at Milwaukee Magazine, and before that spent three years cooking in restaurant kitchens. She believes the fish fry is a civic institution and will defend this position strenuously.

Devlin Park

Arts & Culture Editor

Devlin covers Milwaukee's visual art, theater, and music scenes with the conviction that culture is not a soft beat. He's a former MIAD student, a dedicated attendee of every Skylight Music Theatre production, and one of the few journalists in the city who has actually read the Menomonee Valley Partners' strategic plans.

Ruth Steinberg

Neighborhood History Editor

Ruth is a Milwaukee historian and the author of Gridded: How Urban Renewal Reshaped Milwaukee's Black Neighborhoods (Wisconsin Historical Society Press, 2022). She teaches at UWM and writes The Ledger Room's history coverage with the aim of making the past legible to people who weren't there for it.

Carl Yablonski

Photography & Visual

Carl is a documentary photographer and occasional writer who has been documenting Milwaukee neighborhoods since 2011. His work has appeared in The Guardian and The New York Times. He shoots on film when he can get away with it and digital when the deadline demands it.
